title: [PT Run] Observe clipboard & offer to open http[s]-URLs
body:
## 📝 Provide a description of the new feature

_What is the expected behavior of the proposed feature?  What is the scenario this would be used?_

I find myself frequently juggling with URLs which get pasted to the clipboard and then inserted into some browser-window, so (just as a proof-of-concept) I wrote a little tool (independ of PT) which observes the clipboard and if it finds one, suggests to open - which I can then accept of neglect. I was unsure whether this would be practical of if I would get bombarded with prompts that I don't use. But after a few wks of using this, I still like the idea and would like to take it further - and that is beyond my level of knowledge, beyond the capabilities of the environment I worked on etc., and it also feels like PT Run would be a more obvious home for such functionality. Which is why I opened this issue.

I suggest that PT Run should observe the clipboard and if it finds a new entry commencing with `http[s]:`, it should display a dialog that offers a choice of browsers (either as "found on the system" or configured by the user) which could open this URL. The dialog also has a Cancel-Button. Ideally there should be a configurable timeout after which the dialog will close.

As a milder form (if the observer is disabled through a config-option), it would be good if when entering such URLs into PTs Search-Field there was a choice of browser to open the URL with.

If you'd like to see this feature implemented, add a 👍 reaction to this post.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
@mbaas2 
in what scenario do you copy a URL and then open it in the browser?

Personally I found that is very unlikely that a user will copy a URL and then open a browser and copy that URL in the browser.
Why going through all that when in 99% of the cases you just click or cntrl-click to open it?
When copying a URL is usually to share it through an app (email, chat, messaging etc.)

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: Hmm, I may want to open it in a different browser and  not change the default browser setting. Or it may come from an environment where Ctrl+Click doesn't open URLs. Or it has been opened in one browser but I want to look at it using another browser.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
@mbaas2 
it seems a very limited scenario to justify a pop up that will be interfering every time the URL is copied for other reasons.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: Ok, maybe it's too specific - but as a developer, I need that several times a day.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
@enricogior 
maybe I'm wrong and it's more common than I think.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: I hope some others will jump in to rescue the idea ;)

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: Like sometimes you need to copy an url (from a mail for example) and edit it before opening. So I like the idea

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
@Aaron-Junker 
your scenario is not a match for this feature request, actually it's the opposite.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: "observe clipboard" sounds like a privacy problem to me,if I'm sceptical

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
> "observe clipboard" sounds like a privacy problem to me,if I'm sceptical

If it would be so a big privacy problem, MSFT would not allow to access the clipboard so easely.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: Thanks for all the feedback. I was able to implement that idea in another tool, so I'll close this issue.
